```
**Multi-trial stability** : run scenarios N times to detect flaky/non-deterministic behavior with pass@k metrics
**Release scoring** : a single score combining contract pass rate and behavior similarity

Content:
It is possible to call the MotoServer for tests that were written using decorators. The following environment variables can be set to achieve this:
TEST_SERVER_MODE=true
Whenever a mock-decorator starts, Moto will:
Send a reset-request to `http://localhost:5000`, removing all state that was keptAdd the `endpoint_url` parameter to boto3, so that all requests will be made to `http://localhost:5000`.
Optionally, the http://localhost:5000 endpoint can be overridden by:
TEST_SERVER_MODE_ENDPOINT=http://moto-server:5000
This can be used for example in case of docker-compose configuration that runs Moto server in a separate service container.
Calling the reset-API ensures the same behaviour as normal decorators, where the complete state is removed. It is possible to keep the state in between tests, using this environment variable:
MOTO_CALL_RESET_API=false
```

```
Section Title: Note: pick an appropriate fixture "scope" for your use case > Use ServerMode using the decorators

Content:
It is possible to call the MotoServer for tests that were written using decorators. The following environment variables can be set to achieve this:
TEST_SERVER_MODE=true
Whenever a mock-decorator starts, Moto will:
Send a reset-request to `http://localhost:5000`, removing all state that was keptAdd the `endpoint_url` parameter to boto3, so that all requests will be made to `http://localhost:5000`.
Optionally, the http://localhost:5000 endpoint can be overridden by:
TEST_SERVER_MODE_ENDPOINT=http://moto-server:5000
This can be used for example in case of docker-compose configuration that runs Moto server in a separate service container.
Calling the reset-API ensures the same behaviour as normal decorators, where the complete state is removed. It is possible to keep the state in between tests, using this environment variable:
MOTO_CALL_RESET_API=false
```

Content:
It is possible to call the MotoServer for tests that were written using decorators. The following environment variables can be set to achieve this:
TEST_SERVER_MODE=true
Whenever a mock-decorator starts, Moto will:
Send a reset-request to `http://localhost:5000`, removing all state that was keptAdd the `endpoint_url` parameter to boto3, so that all requests will be made to `http://localhost:5000`.
Optionally, the http://localhost:5000 endpoint can be overridden by:
TEST_SERVER_MODE_ENDPOINT=http://moto-server:5000
This can be used for example in case of docker-compose configuration that runs Moto server in a separate service container.
Calling the reset-API ensures the same behaviour as normal decorators, where the complete state is removed. It is possible to keep the state in between tests, using this environment variable:
MOTO_CALL_RESET_API=false

.

```
Section Title: Schemathesis GitHub Action > Coverage reports
Content:
Schema coverage is powered by [tracecov](https://docs.tracecov.sh) and enabled by default. Each run generates:
A summary in the Actions step summary
An HTML report uploaded as a workflow artifact (default name: `schema-coverage-report` )
A PR comment with the coverage summary (pull requests only)
[](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/1236561/561486757-85c4f138-64f0-434a-938f-e156115853c0.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..SjpbkYwOU0IBCV0XGf4LKt5lC-9-0k4L316i7XtwH5k)
Coverage reports are generated even when schemathesis finds failures.
PR comments require `pull-requests: write` in your workflow:
```
jobs :
  test :
    permissions :
      pull-requests : write 
    steps :
      - uses : schemathesis/action@v3 
        with :
          schema : ' http://example.com/api/openapi.json '
```

GitHub Action that runs Schemathesis tests
GitHub Action for running Schemathesis property-based API tests against OpenAPI and GraphQL schemas. - uses: schemathesis/action@v3 with: # API schema location

```
- uses : schemathesis/action@v3 
  with :
    #  API schema location (URL or file path) 
    schema : ' https://example.schemathesis.io/openapi.json ' 
    #  Override base URL 
    base-url : ' https://example.schemathesis.io/v2/ ' 
    #  Validation checks to run (default: all) 
    checks : ' not_a_server_error ' 
    #  Schema availability timeout in seconds 
    wait-for-schema : ' 30 ' 
    #  Test cases per API operation 
    max-examples : 50 
    #  Schemathesis version (default: latest) 
    version : ' latest ' 
    #  Python module path for hooks 
    hooks : ' tests.hooks ' 
    #  Path to a `schemathesis.toml` configuration file 
    config-file : ' tests/schemathesis-config.yaml ' 
    #  Authorization header value 
    authorization : ' Bearer ${{ secrets.API_TOKEN }} ' 
    #  Additional CLI arguments 
    args : ' --report-junit-path=/tmp/junit.xml ' 
    #  Schema coverage (default: true) 
    coverage : ' true ' 
    coverage-report : ' true ' 
    coverage-report-path : ' schema-coverage.html ' 
    coverage-artifact-name : ' schema-coverage-report ' 
    coverage-pr-comment : ' true ' 
    #  Write coverage summary to the workflow step summary 
    #  set to false when using the action multiple times in one job 
    coverage-step-summary : ' true '

excerpts: Contracts are complementary to API specification documents like OpenAPI. API specifications describe the structure and the format of the API. A contract instead specifies that for a given request, a given response is expected.
Contracts are generated from the expectations defined in the provider mock as a result of a successful test run.

Contracts are not a replacement for a discussion between the consumer and provider team. This is the moment where this discussion should take place (if not already done before). The consumer tests and generated contract are refined with the feedback and cooperation of the provider team.
Lastly the finalized contract is versioned and stored in a central place accessible by both consumer and provider.

**Keeps services decoupled:** Producers and consumers can move independently, as long as the contract holds.
**Prevents breakages across teams:** If you change a response format or remove a field, contract tests catch it before someone else's integration breaks.
Contract testing verifies that a service's implementation matches what its consumers expect.
It focuses on the interface—requests, responses, schemas—not the internal logic.
It's especially useful in microservices architectures and distributed systems, where services evolve independently and ownership is split across teams.
You can use it to verify status codes, response structures, and payload formats based on the contract your team relies on—whether that's an OpenAPI spec, shared schema, or just an informal agreement.

Content:
It is possible to call the MotoServer for tests that were written using decorators. The following environment variables can be set to achieve this:
TEST_SERVER_MODE=true
Whenever a mock-decorator starts, Moto will:
Send a reset-request to `http://localhost:5000`, removing all state that was keptAdd the `endpoint_url` parameter to boto3, so that all requests will be made to `http://localhost:5000`.
Optionally, the http://localhost:5000 endpoint can be overridden by:
TEST_SERVER_MODE_ENDPOINT=http://moto-server:5000
This can be used for example in case of docker-compose configuration that runs Moto server in a separate service container.
Calling the reset-API ensures the same behaviour as normal decorators, where the complete state is removed. It is possible to keep the state in between tests, using this environment variable:
MOTO_CALL_RESET_API=false

Create a change set by submitting changes for the stack that you want to update. You can
submit a modified stack template or modified input parameter values. CloudFormation compares
your stack with the changes that you submitted to generate the change set; it doesn't make
changes to your stack at this point. View the change set to see which stack settings and resources will change.

Change sets don't indicate whether CloudFormation will successfully update a stack. For
example, a change set doesn't check if you will surpass an account quota, if you're updating a
resource that doesn't support updates, or if you have insufficient permissions to modify a
resource, all of which can cause a stack update to fail.

executive_summary.description: A high-level synthesis of the research findings, outlining the recommended design philosophy for Jungle3's stub and simulator layer to achieve high-fidelity, believable enterprise environments.

recommended_fidelity_tier.description: The recommended fidelity tier for Jungle3 v1 stubs, such as 'Integration Grade'.

must_have_elements.description: A list of contract elements that are non-negotiable for achieving the recommended fidelity.

nice_to_have_elements.description: A list of contract elements that are recommended but not strictly required for v1.

validation_artifacts.description: A list of artifacts that should be produced to guarantee replaceability, such as OpenAPI specs or contract tests.

key_risks_of_low_fidelity.description: A summary of the primary risks that could lead to 'plausibility collapse' if fidelity is lowered.

default_policy.description: The recommended default policy for choosing between stateful and stateless stubs.

stateful_criteria.description: A list of criteria for when a stub must be stateful, such as supporting create-read-update workflows.

stateless_criteria.description: A list of criteria for when a stub can be stateless, such as for read-only metadata endpoints.

recommended_persistence_option.description: The recommended default AWS persistence service for stateful stubs, e.g., DynamoDB.

key_plausibility_pitfalls.description: A list of common pitfalls related to state management that can cause plausibility collapse.

recommended_approach.description: The high-level recommended approach for implementing controlled chaos, such as using a proxy layer.

v1_preset_profiles.description: A list of recommended preset profiles for v1, such as 'Stable', 'Realistic', and 'Flaky'.

safety_guardrails.description: A list of mandatory safety features to prevent controlled chaos from becoming actual chaos, like a global kill switch.

reproducibility_mechanisms.description: Mechanisms to ensure that chaotic behavior can be deterministically reproduced for debugging.

recommended_modality_strategy.description: The recommended strategy for providing admin interfaces, such as a hybrid of API, Web UI, and CLI.

core_capabilities.description: A list of essential capabilities the admin surface must provide, like browsing state or injecting events.

recommended_rbac_roles.description: A list of proposed Role-Based Access Control roles, such as 'JungleAdmin' and 'JungleBuilder'.

default_enablement_policy.description: The policy for whether the admin surface is enabled by default and how it can be disabled.

recommended_architecture.description: The recommended architecture for swapping stubs with real integrations, such as a config-flip protected by contract tests.

migration_playbook_steps.description: A list of steps for a safe migration playbook, including shadowing, canarying, and dual-writes.

validation_gates.description: A list of validation gates to ensure a safe rollout, such as consumer-driven contracts and golden flow tests.

observability_requirements.description: Key observability features required for monitoring the swap-out process, like response diffing and correlation IDs.

recommendation.description: The top-level recommendation, e.g., to invest in building a reusable, declarative stub framework.

implementation_strategy.description: The recommended implementation strategy, such as 'Build' using a serverless AWS architecture.

mvp_feature_set.description: A list of minimum viable product features for the framework, like API spec import and state machines.

plugin_model.description: The proposed model for extending the framework with custom domain logic, e.g., via AWS Lambda functions.

recommendation.description: The recommendation on using LLMs, such as adopting a hybrid model but deferring real-time generation.

value_add_areas.description: A list of data types where LLMs provide the most value, such as free-text and narrative fields.

control_guardrails.description: A list of essential guardrails to control LLM output, including schema validation, low temperature, and caching.

reproducibility_controls.description: The primary mechanisms for ensuring reproducibility, such as using Scenario IDs and snapshotting.

failure_patterns.description: The common failure patterns of stubs being 'trusted too much' or 'trusted too little'.

trust_building_mechanisms.description: A list of mechanisms to build durable trust, such as automated contract testing and drift detection.

over_reliance_prevention_checks.description: A list of opt-in checks to prevent over-reliance on stubs, like sunset dates and capability disclaimers.

recommended_documentation_patterns.description: Patterns for documentation that set accurate expectations, such as showing validation status and known limitations.

tool_name.description: The name of the API simulation tool.

primary_language.description: The primary programming language the tool is written in.

key_features.description: A summary of the tool's most important features, such as statefulness or OpenAPI support.

jungle3_fit_analysis.description: An analysis of how well the tool fits Jungle3's specific requirements and deployment model.

recommended_deployment_pattern.description: The recommended AWS deployment pattern for the tool, such as ECS Fargate or Lambda.

prior_art_comparison.description: A comparative analysis of existing HTTP API simulation tools, including WireMock, MockServer, Hoverfly, Prism, and Mountebank. Evaluates their suitability for embedding in Jungle3's per-account AWS deployment based on features, performance, and licensing.

recommendation.description: The core recommendation, e.g., to adopt a hybrid strategy of emulating AWS services and stubbing partner APIs.

emulation_use_cases.description: A list of use cases where full service emulation (e.g., with LocalStack) is recommended.

stubbing_use_cases.description: A list of use cases where simpler API stubbing is sufficient.

plausibility_collapse_risks.description: A list of realism gaps in emulators that could trigger plausibility collapse.

recommended_strategy.description: The recommended hybrid strategy, e.g., using Pact for internal services and Dredd/Schemathesis for external APIs.

tooling_recommendations.description: A summary of recommended tools and their applicability to Jungle3.

ci_cd_validation_flows.description: An outline of the different CI/CD validation flows required for consumers, providers, and external specs.

artifact_strategy.description: The strategy for managing contract artifacts, such as deploying a Pact Broker per customer.

generation_strategy.description: The recommended multi-layered data generation strategy (deterministic, rule-based, LLM-assisted).

persona_catalog_concept.description: The concept of shipping with a pre-built catalog of rich, fictional user personas.

scenario_orchestration_concept.description: The concept of a scenario orchestrator to simulate activity over time, including scheduled events and historical backfill.

versioning_strategy.description: The strategy for versioning seed data, such as treating 'Seed Packs' as versioned artifacts in CI/CD.

safety_guardrails.description: A list of essential guardrails against PII and offensive content in generated data.

observability_pillars.description: The three pillars of observability (Metrics, Logs, Traces) and recommendations for each.

audit_trail_requirements.description: Requirements for an enterprise-grade audit trail, including what actions must be logged.

plausibility_monitoring_heuristics.description: A list of heuristics to proactively monitor for realism gaps, such as data drift and impossible states.

storage_and_retention_strategy.description: The recommended tiered storage and retention strategy for observability data.

versioning_scheme.description: The recommended versioning scheme for contracts and behaviors, e.g., Semantic Versioning 2.0.0.

pre_release_gating_strategy.description: The strategy for validating updates before release, including contract and behavioral testing.

rollout_strategy.description: The recommended rollout strategy for customer upgrades, using CloudFormation Change Sets and feature flags.

deprecation_policy.description: The proposed policy for deprecating old versions of contracts and behaviors.

high_level_principles.description: The core security design principles, such as 'Private-by-Default' and 'Least Privilege'.

iam_recommendations.description: Recommendations for IAM roles, resource scoping, and the vendor support access model.

network_design.description: The recommended network design, emphasizing private subnets and VPC endpoints.

secrets_management.description: The recommended approach for handling secrets, using AWS Secrets Manager and customer-managed keys.

audit_trail_implementation.description: The implementation plan for tamper-evident audit trails using CloudTrail and S3 Object Lock.

v1_actions.description: A list of concrete actions that Jungle3 should take for its v1 release based on the research.

post_v1_deferrals.description: A list of features or actions that should be explicitly deferred to a post-v1 release.

biggest_risk.description: A statement identifying the single biggest risk if the recommendations on this topic are ignored.

cross_links.description: A list of other research topics that have significant knock-on effects from this topic.
